messages:
CI Bot: [ALERT] Canary cluster 'prod-canary' showing spike in 5xx responses for svc-inference route /v1/generate. metric: canary_error_rate=18% (baseline 0.7%). deploy_job=deploy/2026-03-15-08:17.

Oncall Bot: Paging @Jamie H (oncall). Severity: P1 — Canary failing. Please acknowledge.

Jamie H: acked. pulling logs and pod status now.

Jamie H: quick snapshot: canary pods returning 502 and some OOM restarts but kube events show ImagePull and then app errors. seeing `unexpected model load error` in app logs.

Jamie H: checking image digests — the canary deployment image points to tag `release-20260315` which resolves to `sha256:bad123`. our artifact manifest expects `sha256:goodabc`. this smells like a mutable tag got swapped.

Sasha P: I pushed a hotfix yesterday and a post-job script retagged latest -> release-20260315 for staging->prod promotion. Could be a race where builder exposed an intermediate artifact. Mike, any registry syncs or mirror actions overnight?

Mike T: We had a mirror sync at ~02:00 UTC. Pulling registry audit logs now. preliminary: there's a retag event by user=ci-deploy-bot at 02:03 UTC that pointed `release-20260315` -> `sha256:bad123`. I'm seeing the same digest mismatch.

Jamie H: Can we pause traffic? set canary weight to 0 and flip feature flag for the new model. I don't want more customers hit.

Sasha P: flipping flag 'alpha_infer_v2' -> off via flags API.

Sasha P: ``/api/flags/alpha_infer_v2 off`` -> response 200 OK :white_check_mark: traffic should be routed to stable.

Jamie H: pausing canary traffic: `kubectl patch svc route-canary -p '{"spec":{"traffic":0}}' -n prod` — done.

Jamie H: starting rollback of canary to known-good digest now.

Jamie H: ```bash
# rollback canary to pinned digest
kubectl -n prod-canary set image deploy/svc-inference svc-inference=registry.redwood.io/svc-inference@sha256:goodabc
kubectl -n prod-canary rollout status deploy/svc-inference
```

CI Bot: Deploy job 47321 canceled; subsequent rollout halted.

Mike T: registry audit: user=ci-deploy-bot retagged release-20260315 -> sha256:bad123 at 02:03:21 UTC. The bad digest corresponds to a partial build that lacked quantized kernels (caused runtime failures). Also found stale cached manifest on mirror that served the wrong digest to greener regions.

Sasha P: confirming: intermediate image missing kernel-ops lib -> model fails to initialize. This is not a runtime regression in model code, it's an artifact provenance problem.

Mike T: action plan: remove mutable tag `release-20260315` temporarily, prune stale mirror entries, and enforce digest pinning in the CI promotion step. I'll run a prune and then push an immutable alias.

Lina R: I'm up in ~35 minutes. Jamie, what's the latest state for handoff?

Jamie H: canary traffic 0%, rollback complete, new canary pods with sha256:goodabc are ready, health checks green, latency normal. No further 5xx in last 5m. Last affected window: ~02:03:21 - 02:18:00 UTC.

Customer Success: We're drafting customer impact notes. Initial triage: 3 customers reported increased 502s during the window; we're collecting request IDs and will notify affected customers with remediation summary.

Sasha P: proposed long-term fixes: (1) CI promotion must verify release manifest digest == registry digest before publishing tag; (2) disallow mutable tags for production release channel; (3) add a preflight that checks image has required libs/kernels; (4) audit mirror caching TTLs.

Mike T: executing registry prune for mirror and deleting the mutable tag now. Will also create an allowlist that prevents `:latest` style retags to `release-*`.

Jamie H: I've opened an incident ticket and assigned postmortem owners. Short remediation checklist posted to the incident doc.

Jamie H: handoff to Lina in 30m for follow-through on deploy pipeline changes and ensuring CS notifications completed. Lina, please take ownership of follow-ups and postmortem actions.

Lina R: taking it. I'll validate CI guard changes in a dev sandbox and coordinate with Sasha & Mike for production rollout.

Customer Success: Notified customers A, B, C with timeline and mitigation. Will follow up with SLA credit guidance if needed.

Sasha P: adding a CI job to fail if registry digest != manifest digest. I'll open PR and tag Mike & Jamie for review.

Jamie H: closing paging loop — system stability restored. Incident severity de-escalated to P2 while we finish cleanup. Posting final notes to the incidents channel and starting timeline capture. :eyes:
